commits.subject: db: DuckDB 2.0 VARIANT columns are returned as JSON
commits.body:
select * on tables with VARIANT columns crashed the driver or raised an
unsupported type error. The statement is now re-executed wrapped in a
SELECT using positional #n references (so duplicated column names work)
with NULLIF(#n::JSON, 'null'::JSON) for the VARIANT columns, so DuckDB
converts VARIANT to JSON text and a VARIANT NULL is a SQL NULL.

commits.subject: os: moved WinVerifyExeSignature() to mormot.core.os.security
commits.body:
As requested in the PR review: the WinVerifyTrust() wrapper does not use any
feature of the PE unit, so it now belongs to the Windows-only section of
mormot.core.os.security. mormot.misc.pecoff keeps the cross-platform
GetExeSignature() / IsExeSigned() PE parsing.

The WINTRUST_* records use the explicit {$A8}/{$A4} alignment of this unit,
so the FPC-specific {$PACKRECORDS DEFAULT} in mormot.misc.pecoff is not
needed any more.

commits.subject: db: DuckDB 2.0 support - masked FPU exceptions and new column types
commits.body:
- the DuckDB worker threads inherit the FPU flags of the calling thread: with
  the default unmasked FPC exceptions, DuckDB 2.0 raised EInvalidOp - open,
  prepare, execute, fetch, Exec and the Appender EndRow/Flush/Close now run
  between SetFpuFlags/ResetFpuFlags
- unknown type ids made DuckDBVectorValueToText and DuckDBVectorValueToJson
  call each other endlessly (stack overflow): TIMESTAMPTZ_NS (new in 2.0) is
  now a ftDate, GEOMETRY a ftBlob (WKB), and other unsupported types such as
  VARIANT raise ESqlDBDuckDB

commits.subject: ui: pdf - AES-256 on FPC: no wipe of a constant password
commits.body:
On every FPC, EncryptionAes256 and Pdf20File raised an access
violation in TPdfEncryptionAes256.AttachDocument; Delphi passed. The
passwords are wiped with FillCharFast. On FPC, string is an AnsiString,
and StringToUtf8 returns the caller's string itself. So a literal
password such as 'owner' was overwritten in read-only memory.

FillZero(RawByteString(...)) zeroes a string only when its reference
count is 1, and so skips a constant.

Results, now with the AES tests on every compiler:
- Delphi 13 Win32 and Delphi 7: 233
- Delphi 13 Win64, FPC 3.3.1 and FPC 3.2.2 Win64: 230
- FPC 3.2.2 Win32: the known MetafileRenderingAndOrientation #3

Reviewed with Codex.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - EMF text in a GDI path is painted with the path
commits.body:
GDI adds the outlines of text drawn between BeginPath and EndPath to the
path, which its painting record then fills, strokes or drops. The
renderer drew the text at once, in the text colour: an aborted path
still showed its text, StrokePath showed it filled, and FillPath drew it
in the text colour instead of the brush.

Measured with GetPath on a memory DC (Windows 11):
- the text colour is never used;
- an OPAQUE background, an ETO_OPAQUE rectangle, an underline and a
  strike-out each add a rectangle;
- ETO_CLIPPED text adds nothing, and the rest of the path stays;
- after text, the next LineTo starts a figure of its own.

PDF text cannot be part of a path. While a path is recorded,
PathTextOut writes the text to a stream of its own, in a q..Q with its
own Tf, Tc, Tw and Tz, so other text before the painting changes
nothing. It keeps the page's font and spacing for the text after the
path. TextOut writes the rectangles into the path, turned with the text,
and an m back to the current position. The painting records write the
text after their operator, in text render mode 0, 1 or 2 by their brush
and pen; a dropped path drops it. The text is painted after the other
figures, not as one union with them, so the fill rule does not combine
them.

Test EmfTextInPath, 74 checks over eleven cases: FillPath, StrokePath,
StrokeAndFillPath, AbortPath, ETO_CLIPPED, a null brush, an underline,
an opaque background, text in another font after the path, lines around
the text, and a turned opaque background. On master's renderer, 29 of
them fail.

Results:
- Delphi 13 Win32 and Delphi 7: 307
- Delphi 13 Win64, FPC 3.3.1 and FPC 3.2.2 Win64: 304
- FPC 3.2.2 Win32: the known MetafileRenderingAndOrientation #3

This is the same change as in our engine
(martin-doyle/mORMot2-PDF-CrossPlatform#99).

Reviewed with Codex.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: ui: pdf - restore #696 and #695, lost in the merge of #690
commits.body:
Since c12b33766, mormot.ui.pdf does not compile: "Identifier not found
fInLined" at 11 places. #690 merged master into its branch (41b3d0c34),
and that merge took only part of #696. The fInLined field is gone and
TPdfCanvas.NewPath no longer sets fNewPath, but the fInLined uses came
back, and so did the fNewPath resets, the re-force at the end of each
record, and PathBegin/PathClose of before.

The merge also dropped from test/test.ui.pdf.pas:
- the #696 tests EmfNullPenLines and EmfLineAfterEndedPath;
- the MetafileRenderingAndOrientation hash $439DB6C2, which it set back
  to $456748FC;
- one ScreenLogPixels := 96 of #695, in RenderedEmf.

This puts the EMF renderer back to ea5a2bbb6, the master before #690.
It reverses the 15 hunks of c12b33766 from line 11000 on, all in
TPdfEnum and EnumEMFFunc, and restores the tests above. The AES-256 and
PDF 2.0 changes of #690 stay as merged. Against ea5a2bbb6, only those
remain.

commits.subject: soa: release the hold reference manually in ExecuteMethod
commits.body:
A local IInterface variable forces an implicit try..finally block for every
execution of the method: hold is now a plain pointer, released in the existing
finally of HandleCleanup, and in the two early exits where it may be set.

commits.author: Stefan Diestelmann

commits.subject: soa: hold the sicClientDriven instance during ExecuteMethod
commits.body:
A "_free_" call - e.g. sent by a client giving up after its receive
timeout - an instance timeout or a session GC running in another thread
did release the instance while a method was still executing on it,
resulting in a use-after-free in the service implementation.

ExecuteMethod now owns an IInterface reference for the whole execution,
assigned by RetrieveInstance() within the fInstances lock, so
InstanceFreeOrGC() sees RefCount > 1 and defers the actual release to
the next DoInstanceGC() round once the method has returned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HnjnbKNBTbM2GpoD2YuHCC

commits.subject: net: request without Content-Length has an empty body, also with Connection: close
commits.body:
THttpServerSocket.GetRequest only set a missing Content-Length to 0 for keep-alive or GET requests. A DELETE or an empty POST sent with Connection: close and no Content-Length (as Python urllib does) made the server read the body until EOF, so the request hung until the timeout. RFC 7230 3.3.3 / RFC 9112 6.3: such a request has no body.
